deed: לקט ישראל — הצלת מזון וחלוקה לנזקקים
title: Joseph Gitler collected surplus meals from catering halls in his Subaru, and from this grew Leket Israel

trailer.text: Joseph Gitler immigrated to Israel from New York in 2000, and in 2003 he started what became Leket Israel, the National Food Bank.
According to an article, he is an American-born Jew who settled in Ra’anana.
He started alone: he collected meals from catering halls and corporate cafeterias out of his Subaru car.
In 2010 his organization merged with The Leket Food Bank, and Leket Israel was born, which according to an article is an Israeli organization.
In 2024, Leket rescued two million cooked meals from IDF bases, hotels and catering companies, and collected 31,402 tons of agricultural produce.

glance.value: 2 million meals and 31,402 tons of produce

glance.label: Recognition
glance.value: Israel’s representative in the Global Foodbanking Network, since 2011

stations.title: Food in the trash, families without food

paragraphs.text: Joseph Gitler immigrated to Israel from New York in 2000, and soon became acquainted with the poverty statistics in the country.
Catering companies were throwing out huge amounts of food at the end of events.
According to an article, Gitler was shocked at the amount of food waste he saw at weddings and other celebrations.
On his travels around the country, Gitler learned that food was going to waste, that there was no coordinated national effort to save it, and that those responsible for it were willing to donate it.
He said that in organizations dealing with food, almost no one was thinking about what to do with excess or damaged food.
In 2003 Gitler, a new immigrant from New York, started rescuing meals from catering halls, as a one-man volunteer operation.
He collected meals from catering halls and corporate cafeterias out of his Subaru car.
That same year Table to Table, the precursor to Leket Israel, was established.
The goal was to rescue surplus food, prevent waste and help with the problem of food insecurity.
Gitler also went to Canada to study the operations of Second Harvest, a national food bank.
The first warehouse was an old chicken coop, with five standard refrigerators.
Gitler said that from day one it was decided that Leket distributes food to organizations, and does not feed the poor directly.
According to Leket, its sole focus is rescuing healthy surplus food and delivering it to those in need through partner nonprofits.
According to Gitler, the partner organizations are small and struggling, and a large food cost is removed from their budgets.
In 2007 entrepreneur Gidi Kroch joined, bringing logistical skills.
This is considered a turning point.
In 2010 Table to Table merged with The Leket Food Bank, and became Leket Israel, the National Food Bank.
In 2014 a fire broke out in the electrical system of the Logistics Center.
The building burned down with everything that was in it.
Leket moved to a temporary location in Ramot Hashavim, and was operating again within three days.

stations.title: Meals from the army to the schools

paragraphs.text: In 2014 the IDF senior leadership approached Leket and asked for help, because of the huge amount of food being thrown away.
According to Leket, the IDF remains to this day its largest cooked food donor.
The first school to receive cooked food from Leket was the Atid Ofakim High School in the south.
Gitler described a partnership with an army base near Ofakim.
According to him, about 150 children take part there every day in an after-school program.
According to him, the children stay in school, and some of them take the Bagrut (matriculation) exams and serve in better army units.
Noam Lozan, a student who received cooked food from Leket, said that the healthy meals helped him finish his studies and enlist in the IDF.
In Eilat, 19 hotels participate in the program, and a thousand rescued meals are distributed in the city every day.

stations.title: From the field, and in hard times

paragraphs.text: According to Leket, it rescues agricultural produce from over 700 farmers throughout the country.
From surplus produce, Leket makes soups.
It distributes them to people in need, primarily the elderly.
According to an article, almost 100 thousand soup units were distributed to needy elderly people.
In 2020, following the coronavirus, Leket began buying meals from caterers and delivering them directly to elderly people who stayed in their homes.
With the outbreak of the Swords of Iron War, Leket shifted to emergency mode.
It supported residents of the South, evacuees, farmers and nonprofits.
According to the Times of Israel, 228 thousand tons of agricultural produce were lost in the first months of the war.

stations.title: A law, a report and the state

paragraphs.text: On October 23, 2018, after 10 years of extensive lobbying, the Food Donation Act was passed in the Knesset plenary.

The law absolves food donors, non-profit organizations, and their staff and volunteers from criminal and civil liability, provided that they meet the food safety requirements set by the Ministry of Health.
An amendment to the law requires public bodies and government institutions to donate surplus food to organizations that distribute it to vulnerable populations.
In 2016 the first report on food waste and rescue in Israel was published, in collaboration with BDO.
According to the report by Leket and BDO, in 2024 Israel discarded 2.6 million tons of food worth NIS 26.2 billion.
This is 39% of all the food produced.
About half of the wasted food is suitable for consumption and can be rescued, valued at approximately NIS 9.9 billion.
According to the report, about 1.5 million residents, about 485 thousand households, live with food insecurity.
According to the report, every NIS invested in food rescue generates NIS 10.7 in economic value.
According to Leket, since the State Comptroller’s report in 2015 it has led significant change in policy and public awareness.
In 2025 the government launched, for the first time, a national plan to reduce food loss, led by the Ministry of Environmental Protection.

stations.title: Who receives, who does the work, who was recognized

paragraphs.text: Gitler said that Leket feeds not only Jews, but also Muslims, Druze, Bedouins and African refugees.
According to a 2010 article, 20 of Leket's paid staff were Israeli-Arab women who for the first time were earning more than the minimum wage and had full health benefits.
Gitler said that non-Jews see Leket as a Jewish organization, but he wants people to think of it as an Israeli organization.
How many people receive food through Leket each week? The sources give different numbers, from different years.
In 2014 Gitler won the Nefesh B'Nefesh Bonei Zion Prize, in the Community and Non-Profit category.
Gidi Kroch was chosen in 2020 as one of the most influential Jews worldwide.
According to a 2019 article, Gitler called on the new government to increase its funding of Leket, which according to the article then made up 5-10% of its 14 million dollar annual budget.

According to a Leket-sponsored article on the 2021 National Report on Food Loss and Rescue, Israel was ranked last among 18 countries examined in an index of supportive policy for reducing food loss and rescuing food.
According to a report, closing the food insecurity gap through food stamps or direct purchases would cost the government NIS 4.3 billion a year.
Leket’s CEO, Gidi Kroch, called the report’s findings a “national failure”, with no moral, environmental, social or economic justification.
Chen Herzog of BDO called the lack of budget for food rescue “an ongoing failure”, and urged that funding be included in the 2026 budget.

Article sponsored by Leket: in 2024 Leket provided food to over 415,000 people per week

Gitler, when urging increased funding: around 5-10% of the annual budget

claims.text: חן הרצוג מ-BDO כינה את היעדר תקציב להצלת מזון "כישלון מתמשך" וקרא לכלול מימון בתקציב 2026.
claims.quote: He called the lack of budget allocation for food rescue “an ongoing failure” and urged the government to include funding for the plan in the 2026 state budget.

claims.text: גיטלר העריך ב-2019 שמימון הממשלה יהיה כ-5% עד 7% מהתקציב.
claims.quote: In 2019, I think the percentage of government funding will be about 5-7%.

claims.text: הכרה: נציגת ישראל ברשת העולמית לבנקי מזון, מ-2011
claims.quote: GFN Certified Member since 2011

claims.text: חברות קייטרינג זרקו כמויות עצומות של אוכל בסוף אירועים.
claims.quote: We would go to weddings and celebrations of friends and see how much food was being thrown away

claims.text: החוק פוטר תורמי מזון, עמותות, עובדיהן ומתנדביהן מאחריות פלילית ואזרחית, בתנאי שהם עומדים בדרישות בטיחות המזון שקבע משרד הבריאות.
claims.quote: from criminal and civil liability, provided they adhere to the food safety requirements set forth by the Ministry of Health

claims.text: החוק פוטר תורמי מזון, עמותות, עובדיהן ומתנדביהן מאחריות פלילית ואזרחית, בתנאי שהם עומדים בדרישות בטיחות המזון שקבע משרד הבריאות.
claims.quote: absolves food donors, non-profit organizations and staff and volunteers at the non-profit organizations
